scope: Theorem 9.1 of the manuscript “The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global function fields” (preprints/The-Margulis-Platonov-conjecture-over-global-function-fields-October-5-2026/margulis-platonov-global-function-fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 018 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7e90f88648f7bafc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k be a global function field, let L/k be a separable quadratic extension, and let (D, ∗) be a central simple L-algebra of degree n ≥ 3 with unitary involution. Suppose that S = SU(D, ∗) is k-anisotropic. For every integer e ≥ 1, put R = S(k)e , P0 = δA(R), V0 = δ−1 A (P0). Here S(k)e denotes the subgroup generated by the e-th powers, and A is the set of places where S is anisotropic. Then V0 = R.
